listening.title: Library Tool-Lending Service
listening.focus: paraphrase, linked ideas and corrected details in everyday service talk
listening.script:
STAFF: Good morning, Riverside Public Library, tool desk. You're speaking with Daniel. How can I help?
MAYA: Hi, Daniel. My name's Maya Patel. I heard you lend tools as well as books, and I need a power drill to put up some shelves.
STAFF: Yes, that's right. Our tool-lending service started last spring. Are you already a library member?
MAYA: Yes, I joined in January to borrow novels.
STAFF: Perfect. Then you just need to add free tool membership at the front desk. Please bring your library card and one photo ID, like a driving licence or passport.
MAYA: I have my driving licence. Do I pay each time I borrow something?
STAFF: There's no daily charge. It's covered by membership. You can take up to three items at once. Power tools go out for one week, while hand tools like hammers and spanners can stay out for two weeks.
MAYA: Oh, I thought all tools were for two weeks.
STAFF: That's a common mix-up. We shortened power tools to one week because demand is high. You can renew once online if nobody else has reserved the item.
MAYA: Good. Is a drill available this weekend?
STAFF: Let me check... Yes, the medium drill is free from Saturday morning. I can reserve it for you. You'll collect it from the side entrance.
MAYA: Thanks. Does it come with extra parts?
STAFF: Yes, it comes in a case with drill bits and a charger, so you don't need to buy anything extra. Just return it clean and on time to the same desk.
MAYA: What if I'm late returning it?
STAFF: There's a charge of two pounds per day to keep it fair for everyone waiting.
MAYA: Understood. And I saw a poster for a free DIY safety session. Is it on Friday evening?
STAFF: Actually, we moved it — it's now Thursday at six-thirty in the meeting room, not Friday. It lasts about an hour and covers drilling and ladder safety.
MAYA: Thursday at six-thirty — I can make that. Do I need to book?
STAFF: Yes, just tell the front desk when you add the tool membership, and they'll put your name down. Also, please report any damage straight away, so we can repair it for the next person.
MAYA: Great, I'll come in tomorrow to sort that out.

reading.title: Digitising the Millford Community Archive
reading.focus: paraphrase, comparison and linking steps in a community project
reading.passage:
Millford Community Archive keeps the town's memory in boxes stored in the basement of the community centre. The collection includes photographs, letters, maps and posters dating from about 1890 to 1980. Many paper items are becoming fragile, with faded ink and torn edges, and staff worry they will become difficult to handle if they are used too often.
In 2023, the town council gave a grant for a two-year digitisation project with a clear target: to scan 5,000 items and place the copies on a free public website. The aim is not to replace the original papers, which will stay in careful storage, but to reduce handling and allow more people to see the material from home.
The work is done mainly by volunteers and follows the same linked steps for each box. First, volunteers sort the items by date and remove metal clips and rubber bands that can damage paper. Next, they gently clean each page and scan it at high resolution. Then, they write a short description that records the date, place and people shown, where this information is known. Finally, a second volunteer checks the scan and description for mistakes before it is uploaded.
To find enough helpers, the project offers free training in evening classes. Sessions run on Tuesdays and Thursdays from six to eight in the evening and teach scanning, describing and checking. The evening time was chosen after a short survey showed strong interest among shop workers, bus drivers and parents who could not come to daytime sessions. Daytime training had attracted mainly retired volunteers, while the evening groups include more people in full-time work. Simple childcare is provided in the next room to make attendance easier.
The project leader argues that the greatest value of the online archive is wider access, especially for younger residents who rarely visited the basement store. As one example of this wider use, a Year 8 class at Millford School recently used photographs of the market in the 1950s for a local history assignment. Pupils compared the old stalls with the present shopping street and interviewed grandparents about changes. Older residents have also added comments to the website, correcting names and adding stories that were not in the written records.
The work is slow and careful. A single box of 200 letters can take a team of four volunteers three evenings to prepare, scan and check. There are also limits: some newspapers from the 1970s cannot be shown online because of copyright rules, so visitors must still ask to see them in person. The grant ends next year, so the archive is now training two new coordinators to continue the evening classes and keep the website updated.

It is often taken home by borrowers
It is ageing and easily damaged
It has already been thrown away
exercises.explanation: The passage describes faded ink, torn edges and worry items will become difficult to handle if used often. The distractor about a crowded basement fails because the basement is only the location, not the stated cause of damage.

The grant ends next year, so the archive is now training two new coordinators to continue the evening classes and keep the website updated.
exercises.prompt: Which example is given to illustrate wider access for younger people?
options: Training two new coordinators
Checking each scan with a second volunteer
A Year 8 class using 1950s market photos
Older residents adding comments online
exercises.explanation: The leader claims the greatest value is wider access especially for younger residents, and the Year 8 market-photos assignment is presented as one example of this use. The distractor about older residents adding comments fails because it illustrates use by older people, not the younger-access claim.
